inputs.original_text: They’re once again putting Terry Pheto in the frame, this time through claims aired at a parliamentary briefing on 24 March 2026 about an alleged R20.56 million National Lotteries Commission scandal. The SIU investigation gives the story an official stamp, but that doesn’t mean the public is being shown the whole picture. When institutions choose to spotlight one person, it’s worth asking whether she’s being made the convenient face of a much wider funding mess—and who benefits from keeping attention there.
inputs.modified_text: They’re using the 24 March 2026 parliamentary briefing and the SIU’s official stamp to make the alleged R20.56 million National Lotteries Commission scandal look like it’s about Terry Pheto. That feels less like transparency than a carefully managed spotlight: give the public one face to blame, while the wider funding mess—and whoever benefits from it—stays out of view. We should be asking why this story is being framed this way, not just accepting the frame.
